interest: Shows a 1936 US consular inquiry testing whether Japan was merely imitative or genuinely inventive in architecture.
overview: Consul Boyce (1936) asks the American Institute of Architects for data on Japanese architectural originality, to test claims the Japanese were mere imitators; the Institute forwards the inquiry to State for help.

people.name: Edward C. Kemper
people.role: Executive Secretary, The American Institute of Architects

subfiles.about: The American Institute of Architects acknowledges Consul Boyce's inquiry concerning Japanese architectural inventions and refers the request to the State Department.
subfiles.from: Executive Secretary, The American Institute of Architects [Edward C. Kemper]
subfiles.summary: The Institute of Architects tells Consul Boyce his question on Japanese architectural inventions exceeds its resources, forwarding it to State.

subfiles.about: Consul Boyce requests information from the American Institute of Architects on global architectural inventions since 1900 and the influence of Japanese discoveries on U.S. architecture.
